@copilot Update this PR directly with the foundational database-conformance maintainability cleanup described below, preserving its Microsoft SQL Server JDBC feature. Do not create a separate foundation PR or modify any other PR or branch.

The user's request is: "I mean beyond just renovate, I mean in README's, etcetera I noticed the list growing". After discussing the repeated documentation, backend registration/classification, and Gradle project lists, the user explicitly chose: "do the foundational work in the sqlserver PR, leave the others alone, I will focus on getting that one merged first and then rebasing".

Desired outcome: adding another database/client should not require rewriting every shared README introduction, directory tree, command inventory, Renovate filename allowlist, and Gradle project list. Make the shared foundation here for the other database drafts to reuse after rebasing, but do not implement their databases or reorganize those PRs.

1. Refactor scenarios/database/README.md, scenarios/database/java/README.md, and tools/database/runner/README.md so each has one job. The domain README explains package layout, shared contract conventions, and how to run a representative package. The Java README explains Java builds, shared workloads/launchers, and instrumentation modes without repeating the complete supported-backend/client inventory. The runner README documents runner_config.backend, lifecycle, and runner variables without repeating backend names and span-type mappings in prose. Replace enumerated directory trees and every-package command lists with generic layout conventions, links to actual package directories or the authoritative registry, and a small number of useful runnable examples. Do not merely move the same exhaustive catalog into a fourth central file. Do not add a documentation generator or new manifest just for this.

2. Keep meaningful workload descriptions and operational caveats in focused documentation near the relevant scenarios, linked from the shared documentation. In particular preserve JDBC action/contract semantics, Redis workload and telemetry differences, and all SQL Server prerequisites/caveats already present. Move shared JDBC or Redis details into focused workload documentation if that is clearer; do not duplicate that documentation per instrumentation package. Exact dependency versions should remain authoritative in the version catalog/pins rather than be repeated in prose. Keep useful public configuration examples and existing behavior.

3. In .github/renovate.json5 replace the explicit Python database-name alternation with one package-scoped Python-file pattern, for example "tools/database/runner/src/database_conformance/*.py". Retain the existing annotation-based matchStrings extraction and tag/digest behavior. Do not add unrelated compatibility policies or split Renovate into presets as part of this cleanup.

4. In scenarios/database/java/settings.gradle.kts replace the expanding scenario-owned include list with simple deterministic discovery of actual Gradle project build files under the scenario build's owned source directories. Cover the existing shared workload/launcher projects and future backend-local projects without making a database/client list. Preserve existing Gradle project names, explicit mappings for external tool projects, plugin management, and task paths used by conformance.yaml and CI. Do not scan build outputs, caches, nested build trees, or unrelated repositories. Avoid a plugin framework or a new build system.

5. Consolidate backend factory registration and semantic-convention system/span-type metadata so __init__.py and _coverage.py do not require independent duplicate backend inventories. Use one small explicit registry or similarly simple representation, not dynamic import scanning, decorators with import side effects, or an extensible plugin system. Keep backend validation/error reporting and factory behavior intact. Classification must remain restricted to supported CLIENT span types present in the resolved registry; unknown systems and non-client spans must still be ignored. Model backend selectors separately from semantic-convention system identifiers so variants can share a span type, rather than assuming their names always coincide. Reuse the registration metadata for structural consistency checks where useful, but keep independent behavioral expectations in tests so tests can still detect incorrect mappings.

Acceptance: existing PostgreSQL, MariaDB, Redis, and SQL Server conformance behavior and launch task names remain unchanged; the shared documentation no longer grows a new list entry in several places for every backend/client; new owned Gradle projects are discovered deterministically; a backend's construction and span metadata have one explicit registration; annotated Python image pins are still recognized without a new filename allowlist entry. Preserve existing contracts, SQL schemas, stable-semconv gating, and coverage. Add focused regression coverage for registry/classification and project discovery as appropriate, and use the narrowest existing tests/build checks. Apply the relevant Spotless formatting task before Java/Gradle validation and use the repository's Markdown lint runner on changed Markdown. Do not run preliminary spotlessCheck, clean builds, or wait for CI. Leave the other database drafts untouched.

Sequences such as `\a` and `\s` are illegal Kotlin escapes, so the fixture settings fail to compile even after the wrapper invocation is made Windows-compatible. Render the path with `as_posix()` or escape the backslashes before writing it.

threads.body:
The readiness probe passes as soon as `sa` can log in, but SQL Server accepts logins before it has finished recovering `master`/`model` (it can still be in script upgrade mode). `sql_server.sql` then runs `CREATE DATABASE [conformance]`, which needs `model`, so on a slow or cold runner it can fail with e.g. "could not obtain exclusive lock on database 'model'".

To make readiness mean usable, the probe could wait for the databases to come online, e.g.:

```
-b -Q "SET NOCOUNT ON; IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM sys.databases WHERE state_desc <> 'ONLINE') RAISERROR('not ready', 16, 1)"
```

(`-b` matters here, so a query error becomes a non-zero exit.) Also, SQL Server shares the 60s default `_STARTUP_TIMEOUT` with the lighter backends. Its first start is often much slower, so a larger per-backend default might avoid flakes.

For the batch scenario this only checks `db.query.text: present: true`, while the PostgreSQL contract pins the exact sanitized text (`INSERT INTO conformance.items (id, name) VALUES (?, ?)`). If the instrumentation stopped sanitizing the batch and emitted the literal `VALUES (1, 'first')`, this contract would still pass.

Is there a reason the exact text can't be asserted for SQL Server (e.g. the javaagent and library emit different text for batches)? If not, could it be pinned like PostgreSQL, maybe with `db.query.summary` as well?

These discovery tests run real Gradle builds (`--no-daemon`, cold start, up to 180s each, and `test_preserves_database_project_names` configures the whole scenario build) as part of the plain `tools/database/runner/tests` unit suite. That suite runs in the `runner` matrix (including Windows) and in `coverage-model`, which doesn't run `setup-java` and relies on the runner image's JDK.

CI is green today, but this adds noticeable time to each of those jobs, and locally the tests fail with `CalledProcessError`/`FileNotFoundError` rather than skipping when no usable JDK is available. Consider a skip guard like the one in `test_redis_clients.py`, or a marker so only the Java job runs them.

This includes every directory under the root that contains a `build.gradle(.kts)`, pruning only `build`/`buildSrc`/`.gradle`/`out`/`target` and nested builds. A build file used as a test resource (e.g. `.../src/test/resources/fixture/build.gradle.kts`), an Eclipse/Buildship `bin/` copy, or something under `node_modules` would silently become a subproject. The explicit include list it replaces couldn't do that.

Would it be worth limiting discovery to the expected layout (e.g. not descending into `src`, or skipping hidden dirs and `bin`/`node_modules`), or at least documenting the rule in the README?
